source_caption:
Grave of the Fireflies (1988) is one of those films that becomes even harder to watch once you know the story behind it.

The film is based on Akiyuki Nosaka’s semi-autobiographical short story, which was heavily influenced by his own experiences during World War II. Nosaka lost his younger sister to malnutrition during the war, and he later described the story as an apology to her.

That makes Seita and Setsuko’s relationship feel painfully personal. Their story follows two siblings trying to survive in Japan after their home is destroyed during wartime air raids. There’s no grand war narrative here. It’s mostly about two children trying to find food, shelter, and a little bit of normal life while everything around them is falling apart.

There’s also an interesting story behind how the film was released. Grave of the Fireflies was paired with My Neighbor Totoro in 1988. The unusual double feature helped make Totoro possible after its original pitch struggled to get backed. The two films couldn’t be more different in tone, though. One leaves you with warmth and wonder, while the other can leave you completely devastated.

And that contrast may have contributed to Grave of the Fireflies being overlooked by some audiences at the time. After watching Totoro, many people simply weren’t prepared for what came next.

But decades later, the film’s impact hasn’t really faded. It’s a story about two children, but behind them is a real loss that Nosaka carried for the rest of his life.

source_details.synopsis: Grave of the Fireflies (火垂るの墓, Hotaru no Haka) is a live-action TV drama adaptation of Grave of the Fireflies, made by NTV in Japan. It was produced in commemoration of the 60th anniversary of the end of World War II. The drama aired on November 1, 2005. Like the anime, the live-action version of Grave of the Fireflies focuses on two siblings, Seita and Setsuko, struggling to survive the final days of the war in Kobe, Japan. Unlike the animated version, it tells the story from the point of view of their cousin and also illustrates the war changing a kind lady into a hard-hearted woman.
